headline: Govt to ensure full security for Sheikh Hasina if she returns to face trial
summary: Information Adviser Zahed Ur Rahman says ousted PM will be guaranteed all legal and constitutional rights upon her return to Bangladesh.
details: Prime Minister’s Information Adviser Zahed Ur Rahman stated that the government will provide full security to ousted Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina if she returns to Bangladesh.
Zahed noted that Hasina has mentioned returning to the country in December. If she does, she will be brought to trial with all her legal and constitutional rights guaranteed.
The adviser emphasized that everyone must accept the final verdict delivered by the court regarding the cases against her.
Addressing questions about cricketer Shakib Al Hasan, Zahed said Shakib could also return under full security to face the allegations against him.
However, the adviser described Shakib as a "spoiled and rotten person" for his alignment with the previous regime, despite acknowledging him as a good player.
Zahed reiterated that constitutional and civil rights would be guaranteed to all accused, regardless of their political affiliation.
He further stated that the country will not allow any "fascist or mafia regime" to return, asserting that Bangladesh is now a democratic state.
Additionally, he urged people not to speculate on the recent visit of RAW chief Parag Jain to Dhaka, describing it as routine engagement between the two neighbors.
caption:
Full security for Sheikh Hasina? The government says she will be guaranteed all rights if she returns to face trial.

Prime Minister’s Information Adviser Zahed Ur Rahman stated that the government will provide full security to ousted Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina if she returns to Bangladesh.

Zahed noted that Hasina has mentioned returning to the country in December. If she does, she will be brought to trial with all her legal and constitutional rights guaranteed.

The adviser emphasized that everyone must accept the final verdict delivered by the court regarding the cases against her.

Addressing questions about cricketer Shakib Al Hasan, Zahed said Shakib could also return under full security to face the allegations against him.

However, the adviser described Shakib as a "spoiled and rotten person" for his alignment with the previous regime, despite acknowledging him as a good player.

Zahed reiterated that constitutional and civil rights would be guaranteed to all accused, regardless of their political affiliation.

He further stated that the country will not allow any "fascist or mafia regime" to return, asserting that Bangladesh is now a democratic state.

Additionally, he urged people not to speculate on the recent visit of RAW chief Parag Jain to Dhaka, describing it as routine engagement between the two neighbors.

headline_marked: Gaibandha: [[UNO office vandalised]] during protest over family card appointments
headline: Gaibandha: UNO office vandalised during protest over family card appointments
summary: Protesters alleged irregularities in the appointment of 66 information collectors, claiming political bias in the selection process.
details: The Fulchhari Upazila Nirbahi Officer (UNO) office in Gaibandha was vandalised today during a protest demanding the cancellation of the list of family card information collectors.
Protesters, including activists from the BNP, Jubo Dal, Chhatra Dal, and NCP, along with job seekers, staged a procession that led to the destruction of windows in the UNO's room and several chairs.

The unrest was triggered by the publication of a list of 66 appointed information collectors on Monday night, which protesters alleged were appointed in collusion with Awami League and Jamaat-affiliated individuals.
While senior BNP and NCP leaders denied their party's involvement in the vandalism, they claimed that qualified candidates from their parties were ignored in the selection process.
A journalist from the daily Amar Sangbad reported being obstructed and beaten while attempting to record the incident, though NCP leaders denied any involvement in the assault.
UNO Mustafizur Rahman stated that the appointments were made through interviews and IT skill assessments. He added that legal action will be taken against those responsible for the damage.
Fulchhari Police Station OC Durul Hoda confirmed that police were present at the scene and will take legal action if a written complaint is filed.
caption:
Windows smashed and furniture destroyed in Gaibandha as protesters storm a UNO office over alleged appointment irregularities.

The Fulchhari Upazila Nirbahi Officer (UNO) office in Gaibandha was vandalised today during a protest demanding the cancellation of the list of family card information collectors.

Protesters, including activists from the BNP, Jubo Dal, Chhatra Dal, and NCP, along with job seekers, staged a procession that led to the destruction of windows in the UNO's room and several chairs.

The unrest was triggered by the publication of a list of 66 appointed information collectors on Monday night, which protesters alleged were appointed in collusion with Awami League and Jamaat-affiliated individuals.

While senior BNP and NCP leaders denied their party's involvement in the vandalism, they claimed that qualified candidates from their parties were ignored in the selection process.

A journalist from the daily Amar Sangbad reported being obstructed and beaten while attempting to record the incident, though NCP leaders denied any involvement in the assault.

UNO Mustafizur Rahman stated that the appointments were made through interviews and IT skill assessments. He added that legal action will be taken against those responsible for the damage.

Fulchhari Police Station OC Durul Hoda confirmed that police were present at the scene and will take legal action if a written complaint is filed.
